title: I Can Button It

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants to fasten his own bag, but pushing a button flat fails; he turns it on edge, works it through, and repeats the movement.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Pushing a broad flat button straight at its slit does not get it through.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit fastens all three buttons himself after changing his hand movement and persisting.
storyBibleReview.narrator: Kit narrates his growing everyday skill in first person; this does not claim every child must have the same ability.

props: One green satchel with a long flap and exactly three large round yellow buttons in a horizontal row

title: A Turn on the Drum

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Zoe wants Kit to hear her beat, but he plays over it; after she stops he listens and waits, and they answer each other in turns.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Playing both drums at once prevents Kit from hearing Zoe’s pattern.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit holds his hands still, listens, copies Zoe’s beat and pauses for her answer.

title: Back to the Library

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Zoe wants to borrow the fox book that Kit must return today; she accompanies him, waits through check-in, and borrows the returned book.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Zoe asks to borrow the book from Kit, but his library loan ends today and he needs to return it first.
storyBibleReview.resolution: Kit returns the book and Zoe checks it out, giving the same shared book a new reader.

scienceSources.title: Brooklyn Public Library: Borrowing
scienceSources.evidence: Library loans have due dates, and library cards give borrowing access. This fictional loan is due today; the story does not imply children cannot read a borrowed book together or declare a universal loan period.

title: The Hopping Boot

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit wants to put away a boot that hops when he claps; grabbing fails, so he sets a box ahead and uses a clap to pack it.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: The boot slips from his hands; clapping again sends it farther away.
storyBibleReview.resolution: He directs one hop into the box, closes it and waves without clapping.
storyBibleReview.magicRule: The loose red gold-dot boot makes one short forward hop per Kit clap. Speech and waves do nothing; no other object is enchanted.

title: Down to the Sea

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: Where does water in this hill stream go?
storyBibleReview.progression: Follow one connected downhill route from a narrow hill stream through its joining river to the sea.
storyBibleReview.synthesis: The closing view connects the small stream to the large sea through the same river.

scienceSources.title: USGS: Streamflow and the Water Cycle
scienceSources.evidence: Streams and rivers carry runoff downhill; many rivers deliver water to oceans.

scienceSources.title: NOAA: What is a watershed?
scienceSources.evidence: Streams join larger waterways; not all water flows directly to the sea. This book follows one illustrative sea-reaching route rather than claiming every stream does.

title: Feet for Swimming

storyBibleReview.topicQuestion: How do a duck’s feet help it move through water?
storyBibleReview.progression: Move from the paddling duck to one webbed foot, show the push, then return to the whole swimming animal.

oral.prompt: What changed when Zoe sorted again?
oral.listenFor: First the rule was color; then it was size. The same six buttons stayed in use.

visual.prompt: Which group has both red and blue buttons?

title: The Bag with a Patch

storyBibleReview.storySpine: Kit needs to carry blocks, but his cloth bag has a hole; folding the hole fails, so Zoe helps him patch it and he carries the blocks in the same bag again.
storyBibleReview.failedAttempt: Kit folds the torn corner over, but a block slips through as soon as he lifts the bag.
storyBibleReview.resolution: A strong patch closes the hole and the original bag carries the blocks, remaining useful.

scienceSources.title: King County: Reduce, Repair and Reuse
scienceSources.evidence: Mending and repair keep existing products in use rather than immediately replacing them.

oral.prompt: Why did Kit’s second fix work?
oral.listenFor: The sewn patch closed the hole; folding the torn corner did not. He could keep using the same bag.

visual.prompt: Find the part that keeps the blocks inside.
visual.lookFor: The stitched blue patch over the original torn lower corner.

levelRationale: B follows one failed fix and one concrete repair, with familiar objects and short paired sentences. Reuse is shown by the same bag and blocks rather than an abstract environmental moral.
